Our Purpose

The Crusade Mission

Crusade Sports Medicine is a nonprofit organization of UCLA student-athletes dedicated to advancing sports medicine research, education, and equitable access to performance technology.

We conduct meta-analyses and clinical surveys to provide insights on emerging trends in sports medicine — while our engineering division builds accessible wearable devices for all athletes.

Engineering Division

Wearable Sensing
& Analytics

Our custom PCB-based wearable delivers WHOOP-level metrics at a fraction of the cost — designed by UCLA students, for student-athletes everywhere.

Raw sensor data alone doesn't move the needle. That's why every metric feeds our Correlation Engine — a framework that weighs HRV, zone distribution, training load, skin temperature, and gyroscope data together to build a single, honest picture of where an athlete stands.

The output is a Performance Story: not a dashboard of numbers, but a narrative that tells coaches what to act on and gives athletes the confidence to compete — even when the data is complex.

Performance Story
Marcus Chen
UCLA Men's Tennis · #2 Singles · Sophomore
Match Saturday
vs USC · 2 DAYS
Three sensors are telling the same story. The accelerometer: heaviest training week of the season. The temperature sensor: shoulder repairing (+2.2°F, expected and appropriate). HRV: down 9% from baseline — the nervous system absorbing the load.

The other half: gyroscope confirms racket lag up 12%, serve velocity up 6.2%, Zone 4 HR time correlates directly to the improvement. The body adapted. The risk is manageable.

The lever: one more good night of sleep and Marcus walks onto court Saturday at 88% readiness instead of 79%.
You put in the hardest training block of your season — and your serve has never been sharper. That's not a coincidence. The gyroscope confirms it: your racket lag is up 12%. That's the mechanical reason your kick serve now has real bite and your velocity is up 6.2 mph.

Zone 4 data shows your heart has been exactly where it needs to be every time you stepped up to serve at full power. Your body is adapting exactly the way it's supposed to.

Saturday vs USC — your second serve is not a liability. It's a weapon. The data proves it.

8+ hrs sleep tonight. Cap serve reps at 60 Thursday. Shoulder load manageable — protect the form.
Tonight: sleep, eat, recover. Tomorrow: placement focus only. Saturday: trust what the data confirms.

Why We Exist

Our Mission

Advancing sports medicine research, education, and equitable access to performance technology for all student-athletes.

The Organization

Crusade Sports Medicine

Crusade Sports Medicine is a nonprofit organization formed to conduct and publish meta-analyses and clinical surveys to provide insights on emerging trends, practices, and technologies in sports medicine and performance.

We are a highly driven group of undergraduate student-athletes at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) that are passionate about learning how sports medicine is best practiced and what the future will look like for enhancing patient care.

Through our research, we are developing programs that empower teams and individual student-athletes to maximize their potential on and off their playing field, guided by our Crusade 360 values of holistic growth and resilience.

In parallel with our clinical and literature-based research, our engineering division is dedicated to designing accessible, cost-effective wearable sensing technologies that deliver high-quality performance analytics. Our goal is to ensure that student-athletes — including those in low-income and resource-limited communities — have equitable access to advanced tools that support their health, development, and competitive performance.

We are always seeking new members and professionals to join us in building a strong and active community.

Performance Framework

How We Optimize Athletes

SWOT Awareness Metrics

  • Strengths — Identify what each athlete does exceptionally well to build on
  • Weaknesses — Uncover physiological or mental gaps limiting performance
  • Opportunities — Targeted areas where training yields greatest gains
  • Threats — Assess injury risks, burnout patterns, and external stressors

SMART Goal Drivers

  • Specific — Goals tied directly to measurable KPIs
  • Measurable — Tracked via wearable data and clinical assessment
  • Achievable — Realistic milestones based on individual baselines
  • Relevant — Aligned to each sport's demands and position
  • Time-Bound — Scheduled benchmarks across the training cycle

Key Performance Indicators

  • HRV baseline & trend analysis
  • Recovery score + sleep quality
  • Training zone distribution
  • Resting heart rate progression
  • Blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂)
  • Strain load vs. recovery balance
  • Mental readiness self-assessment
  • Injury prevention risk flags

FeaturedZone TrainingEndurance

Zone Training for Endurance Athletes

AuthorCrusade Sports Medicine
PublishedDecember 26, 2024
UpdatedJuly 19, 2025
CategoryTraining Science

Heart rate training zones are intensity-based ranges expressed as a percentage of your maximum heart rate (MHR). These zones provide a structured framework for optimizing workouts — ensuring athletes train with purpose, not just effort. For endurance athletes, understanding and utilizing all five zones is essential to building a well-rounded performance base.

Key InsightHeart rate zones allow coaches and athletes to quantify training intensity, ensure proper recovery, and systematically build aerobic capacity, anaerobic threshold, and speed across a periodized training plan.

Understanding the Five Training Zones

The five-zone model divides training intensity from light active recovery through maximum sprint effort. Each zone elicits distinct physiological adaptations and serves a different purpose within a training program.

Zone% Max HRNamePrimary BenefitTypical Session
150–60%Active RecoveryPromotes blood flow, reduces soreness, enhances recoveryEasy jog, cool-down, active rest days
260–70%Aerobic BaseBuilds mitochondrial density, fat oxidation, aerobic efficiencyLong slow distance, base building runs
370–80%Aerobic ThresholdImproves aerobic capacity, boosts endurance sustainabilityTempo runs, steady-state efforts
480–90%Lactate ThresholdIncreases anaerobic threshold, improves race pace efficiencyInterval training, threshold workouts
590–100%Maximum EffortDevelops VO₂ max, speed, neuromuscular powerSprint intervals, short all-out efforts

Zone 2: The Foundation of Endurance

Zone 2 — often called "the aerobic base zone" — is widely considered the most important zone for endurance athletes. Training at 60–70% of max HR stimulates mitochondrial biogenesis, improving the muscles' ability to use fat as fuel and sustain effort over long durations.

Research consistently shows that elite endurance athletes spend 75–80% of their total training volume in Zone 2. This high volume of low-intensity work builds the aerobic engine that supports all higher-intensity training.

Crusade InsightMany student-athletes make the mistake of training too hard, too often — chronically spending time in Zone 3 rather than Zone 2. This "grey zone" creates fatigue without producing the mitochondrial adaptations of true Z2 training. Use your HRV and resting HR data to gauge when you're recovered enough to push into Z4/Z5.

Zones 4 & 5: Building Speed and Power

While Zone 2 builds the foundation, Zones 4 and 5 create the peak performance capacity. Zone 4 training at 80–90% MHR pushes the lactate threshold — the intensity at which lactate begins accumulating faster than it can be cleared. Raising this threshold allows athletes to sustain faster paces for longer periods.

Zone 5 training (90–100% MHR) is used sparingly — typically comprising just 10–15% of total training volume — but produces significant gains in VO₂ max, sprint speed, and neuromuscular power when combined with an aerobic base.

Applying Zones with the Crusade Wearable

Our wearable device tracks your real-time heart rate and displays your current zone during workouts, giving you immediate feedback on training intensity. Post-session analytics break down your time in each zone, helping coaches and athletes make data-driven decisions about training load and recovery needs.

Combined with HRV and recovery score data, zone distribution analysis becomes a powerful tool for periodization — ensuring athletes peak at competition, not in practice.

Sample Weekly Zone Distribution for Endurance Athletes

  • Zone 1: 10–15% — Active recovery sessions, warm-up/cool-down
  • Zone 2: 60–70% — Long runs, base building, aerobic development
  • Zone 3: 5–10% — Moderate tempo efforts, aerobic threshold work
  • Zone 4: 10–15% — Interval training, lactate threshold sets
  • Zone 5: 5–10% — Sprint intervals, VO₂ max efforts

Key Takeaways

Effective endurance training is not about training harder — it is about training smarter. By distributing effort across the five zones with intention, student-athletes can build a comprehensive physiological foundation that supports both long-term health and competitive performance.

The Crusade approach combines zone-based training with daily biometric monitoring (HRV, recovery score, sleep) to create a fully personalized performance picture — the same methodology used by professional sports organizations, now accessible to every student-athlete.

Engineering Clinical Study Project

Wearable Sensing &
Data Analytics

Our student-led engineering team at UCLA is building a new wearable heart-rate monitor built specifically for athletes. We are collecting athlete feedback to prioritize the data and metrics that matter most in real training environments.

01

Enable Reliable Long-Term Physiological Monitoring

Existing wearables struggle with data feedback & risk analysis during continuous use. We solve that.

02

Build Reproducible PCB Designs for a Scalable Pipeline

Undergraduates learn schematic design, assembly, testing, and robust prototyping for real clinical application.

03

Provide High-Quality Data for Clinical Research

Supporting data collection from UCLA athletes for research publications and performance analytics.

04

Reduce Cost Barriers for Student-Athletes

Most accurate devices are expensive. We aim to develop an affordable, high-performance alternative for all athletes.

Michael Shara
⬡ Hockey · Lebanon National Team Captain
UCLA — Electrical Engineering, B.S. '27
From Orange County, California, Michael is a UCLA Electrical Engineering student and biotech researcher with a passion for innovation in the medical field. His interest in sports medicine stems from his hockey experience working closely with athletic trainers, nutritionists, psychologists, and sports medicine doctors. Before UCLA, Michael took a gap year to play Canadian Junior A hockey in the BCHL, earning the Joe Tennant Most Dedicated Player Award and ranking among the top 10 rookie defensemen in scoring. He now serves as Captain of Lebanon's National Men's Ice Hockey Team and plays for UCLA's Ice Hockey Team. Michael co-founded Crusade to cultivate a community of undergraduate student-athletes passionate about innovating in sports medicine and educating athletes on taking their performance to the next level.
